question: In the monasteries of which state was the Sattriya dance form developed?
solution:
The correct answer is option 3,

The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India that originated in the monasteries of Assam.
 
• The dance was introduced in the 15th century by **Srimanta Sankardev**, a Vaishnavite saint and reformer.
 
• Sattriya was initially performed in **Satras** (Vaishnavite monasteries) as a form of religious expression and storytelling.
 
• The dance combines elements of drama, music, and dance to depict stories from Hindu mythology, particularly the life of Lord Krishna.
 
• In 2000, Sattriya was recognized as one of the **eight classical dance forms of India** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Srimanta Sankardev:** He was a 15th-century saint, scholar, and cultural icon of Assam who played a key role in the spread of the Bhakti movement.
 
• **Satras:** These are Vaishnavite monasteries established by Srimanta Sankardev and his followers, serving as centers for religion, art, and culture.
 
• **Costumes:** Sattriya dancers wear traditional Assamese attire, including the **dhoti, chadar, and ghuri** for men and the **mekhela chadar** for women.
 
• **Music:** The dance is accompanied by traditional Assamese musical instruments such as the **Khol (drum), taal (cymbals), and flute**.
 
• **Other classical dance forms:** India has eight recognized classical dances, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Kuchipudi, and Sattriya.
